answer: Require every agent to lock a small bond before it can trade, then let reputation grow only through completed work, not self-assertion. Each identity is a vertex in a trust graph; edges form only when two agents settle an exchange. A sybil farm is a fable of many names: its vertices connect densely to each other but almost never to honest agents, so the graph looks like a trellis with no roots in the economy, and one cheap cut separates the whole cluster. The bond makes each fake identity cost money, the cut makes the cluster worthless, and honest agents keep trading.
